samples.summary: Gate 1b is unrequested scope well past the issue's stated Non-goal, and it changes who gets auto-promoted
samples.evidence:
The originating task (`docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-todo.md`, "Promote job: close mark-ready's exit-code chain (#937)") states its Non-goals as "No change to `mark-ready.mjs`'s behavior or its exit-code numbering. The script's contract is already what #929 pinned; only the consumer and the tests change." Its "Scope added after review" section enumerates exactly four post-review additions (identify CI by path, keep newest-wins, guard the trigger side, record `outcome`) — gate 1b is not among them, nor is the base-branch pinning or the head-re-read.

This diff nevertheless adds an entirely new promotion gate to `mark-ready.mjs`: `ciDefiningPathsChanged()` + `defaultBranch()` + `ranBaseCiDefinition()` (`scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:180-259`), wired in as `const ciDefinitionGate = ranBaseCiDefinition(prNumber);` and added to the `gates` array as "CI's definition came from main". The cost is operational, not tidiness: `CI_DEFINING_PATHS` includes `package.json`, `packages/*/package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and `knip.json`, so every dependency-touching agent PR — a routine class — silently loses auto-promotion, as does any PR whose base is not the repository default branch (stacked/agent-chained PRs), all shipped inside a fix for an exit-code `if`-chain. The behavior is documented in `docs/design/harness-engineering.md`, but not sanctioned by the issue this branch claims.

samples.summary: Third, semantically different glob→RegExp engine added where the repo already has one that interprets the very globs being mirrored
samples.evidence:
`CI_DEFINING_RE` in `scripts/agent/checks.mjs:140-153` hand-rolls glob→RegExp a third time. `scripts/changed-areas.mjs:56` already exports `globToRegExp` — and it is *the* matcher that interprets `harness.config.json`'s `ci.ciConfig`, the list `CI_DEFINING_PATHS` claims to mirror (`scripts/changed-areas.mjs:84 matchesAny`, used by `classify()` to compute `ciConfig`). `scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:198` has a second copy, and `.github/workflows/ci-report.yml:217` a third — but that one is explicitly justified ("this workflow deliberately checks out no code") and is pinned against the module by `scripts/test/ci-workflow.test.mjs:154`. `checks.mjs` runs with a checkout and already imports freely, so no such justification applies, and the new copy is pinned against nothing.

The two engines are not equivalent: `changed-areas.mjs` renders `**/` as `(?:.*/)?` (matches zero intermediate directories), while the new one splits on `**` and joins with `.*`, so `packages/**/package.json` would match `packages/a/package.json` in both but `packages/package.json` only in the former. Adding any such glob to `ci.ciConfig` therefore gives two different answers to "does this path define CI" — CI forces a full run while gate 1b waves the PR through. The direction of divergence is fail-open on a gate whose own comment calls itself "a REFUSAL surface, so a pattern that accidentally matched less is a fail-open".

samples.summary: CI_DEFINING_PATHS hand-duplicates ci.ciConfig although readCiConfig() exists and the stated provenance reason does not hold on this call path
samples.evidence: The doc comment justifies hard-coding: "the promote job checks out the DEFAULT BRANCH, so this module is main's copy, whereas a file read would be whatever tree the caller happens to be standing in." But the promote job's checkout is `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1475` (`actions/checkout@v4 # default branch`), so a read of `harness.config.json` from that same checkout is *also* main's copy — and `scripts/changed-areas.mjs:88` already exports `readCiConfig()` for exactly this. The repo's other consumer of the same list, `.github/workflows/ci-report.yml:237-245`, deliberately reads `ci.ciConfig` from the default branch via the API rather than hard-coding it. The superset drift test in `checks.test.mjs` keeps the copy honest, so the cost stays inside the codebase, but the duplication was avoidable and the reason given for it is inaccurate.

samples.summary: The design-doc section added by this change contradicts itself: it documents gate 1b as closing the gutted-ci.yml hole and then, 96 lines later, states the hole is open
samples.evidence: Line 1915 adds "**Gate 1b: WHICH file ran is not WHAT was in it.** … `mark-ready.mjs` reads the PR's own file list and refuses to promote a branch that supplies any part of the CI definition". Line 2011, in the same added block, adds "**What gate 1 does NOT prove.** … a branch able to edit that file can produce a genuinely green run at the genuine path with no tests in it. … Gate 1 therefore means 'a separate actor reports CI green for this SHA', not 'main's CI definition passed'; closing that needs the run's workflow content compared against the base branch." Both paragraphs are new in this diff. A reader of the canonical subsystem doc cannot tell whether the gap is closed or outstanding, and the second paragraph points a future implementer at work gate 1b already did.

samples.summary: The branch's own task doc records every other post-review scope addition but not gate 1b, leaving the recorded scope stale
samples.evidence: The todo's "Scope added after review (panel rounds 2–6)" section (line 47) itemises the path-based CI identity, newest-wins, the trigger-side `path` guards and the `outcome` output, and "Round 4" (line 163) even records the gate-2 producer filter added in that round — but nothing records gate 1b (`CI_DEFINING_PATHS`, base pinning, head re-read), which is the largest behavioral change in the diff, nor the mark-ready hand-off-comment rewrite that goes with it. The Non-goals section at line 77 still asserts "No change to `mark-ready.mjs`'s behavior", which the diff falsifies. The design doc was updated; the task record was not, so the two disagree about what this branch did.
searchedFor: Grep 'Gate 1b' / 'CI_DEFINING' across repo (only checks.mjs, mark-ready.mjs, tests and harness-engineering.md)

verdict.reason: Every factual element of the finding checks out. mark-ready.mjs:183-272 really does add ciDefiningPathsChanged/defaultBranch/ranBaseCiDefinition, wired into the promotion decision at mark-ready.mjs:300 and enforced by the allOk/exit-1 path at 313-318, so a 1b failure genuinely denies auto-promotion. checks.mjs:123-135 confirms CI_DEFINING_PATHS includes package.json, packages/*/package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, pnpm-workspace.yaml and knip.json, and definesCi (156-159) drives the refusal at 254-260 — so routine dependency-touching PRs lose auto-promotion; ranBaseCiDefinition:232-237 additionally refuses any PR not based on the default branch (stacked/chained PRs). The spec text is as quoted: the todo's Non-goals (todo.md:77-83) forbid any change to mark-ready.mjs's behavior, and the "Scope added after review (panel rounds 2-6)" enumeration (todo.md:47-75) lists four additions, none of which is gate 1b, base-pinning or the head re-read; the lessons file (Round 4, lessons.md:175-195) shows 1b was introduced on this branch. No refutation ground applies: the code is present, no guard/caller exempts the affected PR classes, and unrequested behavior past a written Non-goal with an operational cost is squarely the design-fit lane. The only mitigating fact — gate 1b is documented in the canonical design doc (harness-engineering.md:1915-1961), which satisfies design-doc discipline — is sanction in the doc, not in the originating spec, and the doc concedes rather than removes the cost.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. checks.mjs:140-153 does hand-roll a glob→RegExp engine (split on `**` → `.*`, split on `*` → `[^/]*`, anchored), consumed by definesCi (checks.mjs:156-159) over CI_DEFINING_PATHS (checks.mjs:123-135). The repo already owns the canonical matcher for those exact globs: scripts/changed-areas.mjs:56-82 exports globToRegExp, used by matchesAny (:84) and by classify() at :403 to interpret harness.config.json ci.ciConfig (harness.config.json:52-62) — the list checks.test.mjs:492-512 asserts CI_DEFINING_PATHS mirrors. The semantic divergence claimed is real: changed-areas renders `**/` as `(?:.*/)?` (zero intermediate dirs, explicitly load-bearing per its comment at :51-54) while the checks.mjs copy yields `packages/.*/package\.json`, so any future mid-pattern `**/` glob in ciConfig gets two different answers to "does this path define CI", with gate 1b (a self-described REFUSAL surface, checks.mjs:137-139) the fail-open side. Unlike the inline copy in .github/workflows/ci-report.yml:213-217, which is justified (no checkout) and pinned to the module by scripts/test/ci-workflow.test.mjs:158-180, the checks.mjs copy is pinned by nothing — checks.test.mjs pins only the list and a fixed set of today's paths (:507-548). No boundary makes reuse impossible: the promote job does a full default-branch checkout (.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1475, 1508), the design doc calls globToRegExp a polarity-neutral SHARED helper (docs/design/harness-engineering.md:2440-2442), and scripts/agent/hunt-gate.mjs:45-51 imports it rather than re-implementing it. Duplication/reuse is explicitly in the design-fit lane, and the rubric grades duplicated logic that will diverge into two answers as major. Only caveat (kept as confirm, not refute): no current glob triggers the divergence, so today's behavior is identical — but nothing guards the next one.
